Apple doesn’t publish a base price in the release notes, so the current cost is on the Apple store or authorized resellers; you’ll see the retail price there.  

If you’re on an iPhone 14, the upgrade gives you a new **A20 Pro** chip, variable‑aperture camera, longer battery life, built‑in Siri AI, and satellite connectivity for emergency use [3].  
Trade‑in credit for an iPhone 14 can be as high as **$1,200** [3], which can offset a large part of the new model’s cost.  

So, for a user who wants the newest camera tech, battery, and AI features, the **iPhone 18 Pro** is a worthwhile upgrade. If your iPhone 14 still meets your daily needs, the jump may not be necessary.

answer_raw:
The newest iPhone lineup is the **iPhone 18 Pro** and **iPhone 18 Pro Max**, released on **September 18, 2026**. The **iPhone Duo**, released on **October 23, 2026**, is Apple’s first foldable iPhone. [4]. Apple hasn’t published a retail price in the announcement, but it offers a leasing program that starts at **$57.99 per month for 24 months** [4].

Apple also launched the **iPhone 18 Pro** and **iPhone 18 Pro Max** on **September 18 2026** [3]. No retail price is listed in the announcement, so you’ll need to check the Apple Store or an authorized reseller for the current cost.

For someone on an iPhone 14, upgrading to an iPhone 18 Pro gives you:

* the new **A20 Pro** chip,
* a **variable‑aperture camera** system,
* longer battery life,
* built‑in **Siri AI**, and
* **satellite emergency connectivity** [3].

Trade‑in credit for an iPhone 14 (or any newer model) can be as high as **$1,200** in the U.S., which can offset a substantial part of the new device’s cost [3].

Whether the upgrade is “worth it” hinges on how much you value those new features and how well your iPhone 14 still serves you. The 14 remains fully supported, but the 18 Pro’s performance, camera, AI, and emergency satellite functions are significant improvements that many users find compelling. If you’re satisfied with the 14’s current performance, the upgrade may be optional; if you want the latest hardware and capabilities, it’s a worthwhile move.
